definitions.gloss: bothersome; tiresome; annoying; what a hassle
definitions.explanation: Describes something that requires more effort or trouble than one wants to deal with. Stronger and more colloquial than 面倒.

examples.japanese: {掃除|そうじ}が{面倒臭|めんどうくさ}い。
{面倒臭|めんどうくさ}い{手続|てつづ}きが{多|おお}すぎる。
examples.english: There are way too many tiresome procedures.

examples.japanese: {毎回|まいかい}パスワードを{入力|にゅうりょく}するのが{面倒臭|めんどうくさ}くて、{指紋|しもん}{認証|にんしょう}に{変|か}えた。
examples.english: Entering my password every time was such a pain, so I switched to fingerprint authentication.

notes:
{面倒臭|めんどうくさ}い is an い-adjective. It is a stronger, more colloquial version of {面倒|めんどう} (na-adjective meaning "troublesome").

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {面倒臭|めんどうくさ}く
- Casual contraction: めんどくさい (very common in speech)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {面倒|めんどう}: troublesome — neutral register, also used as a noun
- {煩|わずら}わしい: annoying, vexing — slightly more formal, emphasizes emotional irritation
- {厄介|やっかい}: troublesome, burdensome — implies the problem is difficult to deal with

The casual shortened form めんどくさい is extremely common in spoken Japanese and is not considered rude among friends, though the full form {面倒臭|めんどうくさ}い is preferred in writing.
